facts.statement: The genus Artiodus is monotypic, containing only the single species Artiodus prominens.
facts.quote: It is currently monotypic, containing only the species Artiodus prominens

facts.statement: The evolutionary affinities of Artiodus remain unclear, a common issue for many Paleozoic cartilaginous fish genera.
facts.quote: As with many Paleozoic chondrichthyian genera, its affinities are unclear at this time.

facts.statement: Fossils of Artiodus prominens have been found in the Early Permian deposits of the Middle Urals in Russia.
facts.quote: from the Early Permian of the Middle Urals of Russia

facts.statement: Artiodus lived during the Artinskian stage, between 290.1 and 283.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Artinskian to Artinskian (290.1 to 283.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: Artiodus is classified within the parent group Euselachii.
Artiodus belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
